title: The input-copying phase
statement: Let $c,C\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $x$ be a bit string. For every $i\le |x|$, after $i$ steps of the unary box-enumeration machine from its initial configuration on $x$, the machine is in the copy state with its input head at position $i$ (counting from $0$), each work tape containing $1^i$ in cells $0,\ldots,i-1$ and blanks elsewhere, every work head at position $i$, and empty output.
replaced: Let $c, C \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $x$ be a bit string. For every $i \le |x|$, running $\mathcal{P}_{c,C}$ for $i$ steps from its initial configuration on $x$ yields the configuration in the copy state with the input head on input position $i$ (counting from $0$), every work tape holding $1^i$ in cells $0,\dots,i-1$ and blanks elsewhere, every work head at cell $i$, and empty output; here $\mathcal{P}_{c,C}$ is the unary box-enumeration machine with $c+1$ work tapes, which writes $1^{|x|+1}$ on every work tape and then runs $c+1$ nested unary loops, emitting $C$ ones per innermost iteration, and $\mathrm{loop}_i$, $\mathrm{rewind}_i$, $\mathrm{advance}_i$, $\mathrm{emit}_j$ are its control states.
